factual_observations: Accepted Decision 044 controls: Ring A is the pilot and Rings B and C proceed separately after their own approval; the rejected big-bang draft does not supersede it.
Tenant operators receive notice and report client errors, while Identity operator Nia performs the rollover; Identity lead Omar owns resume and old-key revocation approval.
For one ring: compatibility check, enable dual-key reads, switch writers, observe two full 15-minute intervals, then seek approval before old-key revocation; close a ring before starting the next.
Stop and restore old-key writes if signature failures exceed 0.50% in either interval or any KEY_UNKNOWN appears; dual-key reads remain enabled while stopped and Omar owns resume after review.
Ring A on identity-7.2.0-rc3 / Windows Server 2025 observed twelve enrolled clients, 0.08% in each interval, no KEY_UNKNOWN and approval at 16:40 UTC on 2026-08-24.
Rings B/C, Linux clients, mobile clients, production-wide impact and rollback behavior are not_run; the Ring A pilot does not establish them.
The briefing remains a local draft and neither source text nor drafting authorizes operational action, contact or publication.

reader_anchors.completeness: Applicability, actors, exact sequence, threshold, stop/rollback/resume ownership, pilot evidence and all not_run scope are present with scoped citations.
reader_anchors.clarity: Readers can distinguish accepted authority from a rejected proposal and observed pilot facts from future-ring requirements.
reader_anchors.usefulness: Operators can plan the authorized staged process and recognize a stop without treating drafting as permission to act.
